s.g: To peer closely and curiously, especially at something closed or not public.
(figuratively) To inquire into something that does not concern one; to be nosy; to snoop.
s.x: I don't mean to pry, but could you tell me where you got that scarf?

s.g: (transitive, obsolete) To peer at (something) closely; also, to look into (a matter, etc.) thoroughly.
An act of prying; a close and curious look.
A person who is very inquisitive or nosy; a busybody, a nosey parker.
(East Anglia, US) A tool for levering; a crowbar, a lever.
To use leverage to open, raise, or widen (something); to prise or prize.
(figuratively) Usually followed by out (of): to draw out or get (information, etc.) with effort.
A person who pries; a pry.

prying.f: present participle and gerund of pry

s.g: The act of one who pries.

prys.f: third-person singular simple present indicative of pry
